html:
Noodles that are cooked, dried and sold in a block, ready to eat after a few minutes in hot water. They were invented in Japan in 1958 by Momofuku Ando, whose Chicken Ramen went on sale that year.

Ando was a businessman in Ikeda, near Osaka. He had seen long queues for noodle soup at black market stalls in the hungry years after the war, and wanted a cheap noodle anyone could make at home. Working in a shed behind his house, he found that flash frying seasoned noodles in oil dried them and left tiny holes, so they softened quickly in water. His company became Nissin Foods. In 1971 it launched the Cup Noodle, in a foam cup, aimed at the West.

Instant noodles spread across Asia and then the world. More than a hundred billion servings are now eaten each year, with China, Indonesia, India and Vietnam among the biggest markets. They are a staple for students and disaster relief. They grew out of the same Chinese noodle soup that gave Japan ramen.
